title: You did not throw
hookLine: at Badr, you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw (8:17)
tomorrow: Between a man and his heart

cards: An award show. The winner reaches the microphone and starts thanking people: my coach, my mom, the team, the crew. Some of it is politeness.
But often there's something true in it: the trophy has their name on it, and it was never only them. At Badr, the sources say, the Muslims were badly outnumbered.
Commentators report that as the battle began, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ picked up a handful of pebbles and dust and threw it toward the other army. Afterward, a verse came about that throw.

teach.h: WA MA RAMAYTA — YOU DID NOT THROW.
teach.b: Verse seventeen begins with the believers: you did not slay them, but Allah slew them. Then it turns to the Prophet, in Pickthall's words: “thou (Muhammad) threwest not when thou didst throw, but Allah threw.”
In Arabic it's almost a riddle: wa ma ramayta idh ramayta, wa lakinna Allaha rama. You did not throw, when you threw. The verse doesn't deny that the Prophet's arm moved.
It says you threw, and in the same breath, it wasn't you.

teach.h: THE HAND WAS HIS; THE REST, ALLAH'S.
teach.b: In the verse's telling, both are true at once: the hand was his; the reaching of that handful, and what came of it, was Allah's. The verse goes on: that He might test the believers with a good test from Him.

Even victory is a test. Will you say, look at us? The surah opened with an argument over the spoils, and this verse quietly answers it: if the win wasn't only yours, the spoils aren't only yours either.

Muslim theologians have long argued over how a human act can be both truly yours and truly from God; different schools gave different answers, and the debate is still taught. The everyday lesson teachers draw is simpler.
Effort is real, and it matters.
Success is a gift, and it humbles. After good news, a job, a grade, a recovery, Muslims say alhamdulillah, praise be to God. In a way, it's this verse in one word.

how: Muslims often answer praise or good news with alhamdulillah or ma sha' Allah, and teachers cite 8:17 to explain why success is credited to Allah while effort is still expected.

games.q: you've just won against the odds. everyone's congratulating you. what does 8:17 point you toward?
o: take full credit. you earned it.
own the effort, and credit Allah for the outcome.
say you did nothing at all.
games.why: you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw: the act was real, and the outcome a gift and a test.

practice: Think of one thing you're proud of from this week or this year, and let yourself feel the effort you put in, because it was real.

Then widen the picture: the health that let you do it, the people who taught you, the timing you didn't control, the breath in your lungs. If you pray, say alhamdulillah for it; if not, simply credit what wasn't you.

wordCard.voice: Rama, threw. Surah eight, verse seventeen: you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw. The hand was the Prophet's; the outcome was Allah's. Today's word.
